message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in males. The gene responsible for mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—male lions with at least one copy of the dominant allele will develop a mane, while females (who lack the Y chromosome) do not. This trait is a classic example of sex‑linked dominance in felids.
